result:
PR #309 is marked ready at `4ef1300091`. Neither candidate fix restores Ghoulies' frame rate, and the soaks refute the idea that TLB-walk overhead causes the #311 collapse.

**Why the previous session hadn't finished:** it had stopped on purpose to wait for the seven Thor soaks and the two pixel comparisons. All of them had landed by this resume, so this session judged them.

**Verdict (Thor, 240 s hands-off, one run per arm):**

| arm | Ghoulies frame rate, 90–240 s | Crimson Skies |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline (counters only) | median 2 fps, down from 29 | — |
| (b) cap the TLB size | median 2 fps: fails its prediction | 29 fps, no crash |
| (a) keep emptied pages armed | **no result** | 29 fps, no crash; the expensive walks drop from ~1100 to ~5 per 2 s |

- **The model is refuted.** In the baseline the frame rate collapsed while the cost per walk stayed flat (1.07x from 22 s to 121 s). The TLB never grew past 4096 entries. The walks took only 0.8% of a guest thread that was busy about 97% of the time.
- **(a) has no Ghoulies result, and it was not a crash.** The soak script's liveness check is an `adb shell ps`. At 15 s it failed on a known connection error (`UtilAcceptVsock accept4 failed 110`), and the script read that as the game exiting. Logcat shows the game still running when capture stopped. I didn't re-queue it: at 0.8% of guest CPU, removing every walk can't take 2 fps to 25.
- **Pixels:** 0 of 593 rows differ on either hunk.
- **JSRF was never tested:** both runs errored because the title isn't on the Thor.

**What I changed this session:**
- Turned (b) back off. The branch head had it on, and folding would have shipped a hunk that failed its test. Both hunks are now off at the head, so the PR lands only the `[tlb68]` counters. Each hunk's test commit stays on the branch.
- Merged origin/master in; it merged cleanly.
- Wrote the verdict into `docs/lanes/tcgchurn/NOTES.md`, updated the PR body (`Files:` matches the diff), and posted the verdict on #311, #68 and the PR.

**For #68:** on these soaks at current master, `tlb_reset_dirty` takes 0.4–1.7% of guest CPU and the jump-cache wipes 0.2–0.3%. The 09-11 profile the brief cites had 10.68% and 8.37%, but it predates #73's fix. These are hands-off soaks, not Crimson's heavy-flying route, so NOTES recommends a fresh heavy-flying profile before any further #68 fix.

**Preflight** passes except the `coverage` gate. It fails because the board's tracker still lists #311 as open while GitHub has it closed; that file belongs to the board, so I left it alone.

CI on the new head hasn't run yet.
